newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Algeria's ruling FLN backs constitution.
newsitem.headline: Former Algeria's ruling FLN backs constitution.

text.p: Algeria's former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) party on Wednesday urged people to approve the November 28 referendum to amend the constitution.
The FLN said in statement that the proposed constitution would help establish multi-party democracy in the North African oil and gas producing country.

The FLN ruled Algeria from independence in 1962 until nationwide riots in 1988 forced the party to agree to multi-party rule. But Algeria erupted into violence early in 1992 when the authorities cancelled general election in which the now banned radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a huge lead.
"The draft establishes the multiparty democratic choice through a huge balance of the executive branches of power and guarantees more respect for freedoms and human rights," said the FLN.
The draft bars parties from using Islam for political gains.

Two legal Islamist parties, which will have to change their platforms to stay legal under the planned constitution, have said they oppose the referendum but have not given instructions to their backers on how to vote.
The two parties argue it will only worsen divisions among Algerians following nearly five years of civil strife in which more than 50,000 people have been killed.
Two main secular opposition parties, the Socialist Forces Front and the Rally for Democracy and Culture have told their supporters to boycott the referendum or vote "no".
They argue the draft does not give equal weight to the Berber language and will set the stage for constitutional dictatorship.
